title: KV + prefix cache recommendations: hit-rate modeling, TTL policy, key hygiene, and safe automated apply/rollback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: produce a prescriptive, implementable set of KV/prefix cache recommendations for Redwood runtime to (1) model expected hit-rate uplift from key design and TTL policies, (2) specify adaptive TTL and policy heuristics, (3) define cache-key canonicalization hygiene, and (4) define an automated, safe apply + rollback workflow for policy changes. Scope: runtime KV/prefix caches used for prefix-KV caching and short-term prompt snippet caching across hosted and dedicated deployments. Excludes long-term offline caches and embedding caches stored in external DBs. Deliverables: modelling notebook, config validator, canary rollout plan, runbook for rollback, sample GitOps config fragments, and a 2-week pilot on dedicated pool A.
decision: Adopt adaptive per-prefix TTL using observed inter-arrival time (IAT) percentiles + global floor/ceiling. Use conservative canary (1% traffic -> 10% -> 100%) with automated rollback triggers tied to cost, latency, and quality metrics. Enforce canonicalization rules for keys and include model-version metadata in key namespace to avoid stale cross-variant pollution.
acceptance_criteria: Model predicts >=10% tokens-per-request cost reduction for pilot workload or explains why not
Config validator rejects policies that remove model-version from key namespace
Pilot canary applied to dedicated pool A and rolled back automatically if metrics exceed thresholds
Runbook and alerting present for rollback and manual remediation
rollout_plan: Step 0: Dry-run analysis in notebook using 14-day request traces; produce simulated hit-rate curves per prefix
Step 1: Deploy config validator to infra-config repo; block PRs that violate key hygiene rules
Step 2: Apply policy in dry-run mode (no writes) for 1% traffic on dedicated pool A for 48h
Step 3: If dry-run metrics match simulation, enable writes for 10% traffic for 72h and run eval sampling
Step 4: If canary passes, promote to 100% for that pool and schedule cross-pool rollouts
rollback_plan: Automatic: feature-flag revert if any of the following breach within the canary window: cache.hit_rate_drop > 5% absolute, tokens.per_request reduction < 0 (i.e., cost increased), p95 latency increase > 10% or semantic-similarity drop on eval sample > 0.02
Manual: run runbook to revert infra-config PR, invalidate affected cache namespaces, and trigger hotfix rollout
Post-rollback: capture full trace dump for root-cause analysis and follow-up patch
